reason: I want to build the pump, and heart muscle looks suited to the pumping walls slot.

reason: I want to complete the chamber's direction control, and valves appear suited to that role.

effect: The valves provide direction control by responding to pressure, and the chambers now have both pumping walls and valves.
reaction: The explanation makes the valves' role clear.
reason: I want to give the pump a rhythm, and pacemaker cells appear suited to that job.

reason: I want to make the fluid that will fill the circuit, and plasma and red blood cells are components of blood.

reaction: The separate roles of plasma and red blood cells are clear.

reaction: The distinction between moving blood and exchanging substances with tissues is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and veins should add the return route.
expectation: I expect the veins to complete the vessel circuit, which may still need the blood and heart connected.

effect: The veins complete the vessel route back toward the heart; the circuit still needs blood and a pump.
reaction: The returning route makes the circuit easier to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and adding blood should fill the vessel circuit.

effect: The vessel circuit is now filled with blood, and the remaining goal is to connect it to the pump.
reaction: The construction makes the pump's relationship to the returning route easy to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting the heart should let it move blood through the circuit.
expectation: I expect a working circulation system that moves blood through the vessels and back to the heart.

effect: Connecting the heart completed circulation and showed how the pump and returning route work together to deliver blood to distant tissues.
reaction: The completed circuit was satisfying, and the explanation tied its parts together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the heart to the filled circuit brought the separate constructions together and clarified why tissues need both a route and a pump.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the circuit felt predictable after the blood and vessels had been made, although it helped show what the pump would move.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that cells in the heart start its repeating rhythm without a separate brain command for every beat.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the parts had clear roles, though several later combinations were the only options offered.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter: the construction and explanations made me curious about how the connected systems support the arm.
